verdict.rationale: Anytype's own docs say the vendor cannot see user content and that data can stay entirely on-device or on a self-hosted network, which structurally keeps the vendor from training models on it. However, no document explicitly addresses AI-training use, and community reports about encryption at rest concern local disk storage rather than vendor access. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party policy stating user data is never used for AI training, a documented opt-out or control specific to AI training, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

citations.quote: Only you can access your spaces and grant access to others — not even Anytype can see your content.
If you prefer to fully keep your data on your device without any server to sync between your desktop and mobile, you can enable local-only mode.
All your content is stored locally on your device
Only you, and the people you choose to share with, can read it.
